title: Audit logs & admin activity review - Verdant Bank
summary: Redwood AE+SE reviewed audit logging and admin activity features with Verdant Bank. Covered what events are captured, retention and export options (S3, SIEM, syslog), integrity/signing, KMS/HSM encryption, RBAC/SSO integration, data residency concerns, and SOC2/ISO artifacts. Agreed to send log schema, SOC 2 report, and schedule a technical deep dive and POC for log forwarding to Verdant SIEM.
topics: what audit logs capture (admin actions, API calls, config changes)
export options: S3, syslog, webhooks, Kafka, Splunk/Elastic connectors
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-22 14:00 UTC
Duration: 46m
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Sam (Redwood Security), Matt (Verdant CISO), Dina (Infra), Omar (Compliance)

Summary (auto): quick run through of audit logs, retention, export and next steps to share artifacts.

[00:00] Alex (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros?
[00:08] Matt (Verdant): Matt here, CISO at Verdant Bank. We're primarily concerned with what you capture in audit logs for admin activity, retention and how we can ingest into our SIEM.
[00:18] Alex: Got it. Priya and Sam from the product/security side are with me. We'll go through schema, export options, retention controls, and integrations.
[00:28] Priya (Redwood SE): To start, our audit logs capture admin logins, role changes, SSO events, API key creation and deletion, model deployments, config changes like routing and retention updates, and prompts to the degree required for debugging (redaction by default). We also log request metadata - IP, user-agent, request id, route, and resource identifiers.
[00:50] Dina (Verdant): When you say prompts, do you store plaintext prompts in logs? Compliance requires minimal retention for any sensitive PII.
[00:58] Sam (Redwood Sec): Good question. By default we do not persist full request payloads in the admin audit index. We have a separate request-level debug log that can be toggled per account for POC/troubleshooting; it's encrypted at rest and we recommend redaction. Customers can opt-out or set TTLs.
[01:16] Omar (Verdant): Can you confirm the schema fields? We need timestamp, actor, action, target resource, before/after state, IP, geo, request id, and an immutable event id for chain of custody.
[01:28] Priya: Yes, schema contains timestamp (ISO8601), actor (user id / service principal), action (string), target (resource type + id), outcome (success/fail), metadata blob (IP, user-agent), and change delta where applicable. We also surface a UUID event id. I'll share the full JSON schema after.
[01:45] Matt: Is the event id signed? We need integrity guarantees for audits.
[01:50] Sam: We support log signing at export time — HMAC-based signing for S3 exports and can integrate with our HSM-backed KMS for signing keys. For high-assurance customers we can provide a signed manifest per export.
[02:03] Alex: Also, we keep an append-only internal store for a configured retention window; deletions are soft first and then purged based on retention policy unless a legal hold is in place.
[02:13] Dina: What are export options? We run Splunk and have a Kafka pipeline.
[02:18] Priya: Export options: native delivery to customer S3 buckets (with encryption SSE-KMS), syslog/webhook endpoints for real-time streaming, Kafka connector, and direct integration with Splunk/Elastic via connectors. We also support periodic batch exports (daily/hourly) and live forwarding for high-volume streams.
[02:36] Omar: For S3 delivery, can we use our KMS keys?
[02:39] Sam: Yes, customers can use their own KMS keys (customer-managed keys). We support AWS KMS CMKs, and for on-prem or higher assurance we support HSM integrations for key policy enforcement.
[02:51] Matt: Data residency — our policy requires logs to stay in EU regions.
[02:55] Alex: Redwood supports region-pinning for storage and export. If you require EU-only, we can ensure logs are stored in EU buckets and exports originate from EU endpoints. We'll note the exact region constraints in the architecture doc.
[03:10] Dina: Retention — what's configurable? Our compliance needs 7 years for certain events.
[03:15] Priya: Retention is configurable per event type. Default admin logs 1 year, security logs 7 years (configurable), request-level debug shorter. We can support legal hold to prevent purging; however very long retention may have cost implications which we can surface in pricing.
[03:33] Matt: Are deletions audited? We need to see who deleted logs and why.
[03:37] Sam: Yes, deletions and retention policy changes are themselves logged as immutable events, including actor and reason. Those events are stored for the full audit window.
[03:44] Omar: How do we integrate SSO/RBAC context so the logs show the user's directory identity?
[03:49] Priya: We map SAML/OIDC identities to Redwood user ids. When you enable SSO (Okta/Azure AD), our logs include both the federated identity (email, external id) and the internal actor id. Role changes via RBAC are tracked with before/after role assignments.
[04:06] Dina: Any limitations with service principals or API keys?
[04:09] Priya: API keys are tied to service principals; actions taken via keys are logged with the principal id. We also capture the originating IP and token id. For high-sensitivity operations, we recommend MFA and scoped service principals.
[04:21] Matt: For SOC 2 / ISO evidence, do you provide artifacts?
[04:25] Alex: We can provide SOC 2 Type II report, ISO 27001 certificate (where applicable), and a package with control mappings and screenshots. Sam will own the security pack delivery.
[04:36] Sam: I'll share our SOC 2 report and a log ingestion test plan. Also include sample signed manifests and the schema.
[04:43] Omar: We want an automated ingest test — a small POC where you forward a set of events to our Kafka and we validate schema and signing.
[04:52] Priya: That's straightforward — we can spin up a POC pipeline, forward both real-time and batch exports. We'll include examples for Splunk HEC as well.
[05:02] Dina: Are there quotas or throttling on export? We ingest high-volume logs; need to ensure no drops.
[05:08] Priya: We have burst capacity for exports. For sustained high volumes we recommend a dedicated export stream or using our Kafka connector which is backpressured. We'll include throughput numbers in the follow-up doc.
[05:20] Matt: What about log integrity during transit? TLS, mutual TLS, cert pinning?
[05:26] Sam: All exports use TLS 1.2+, and for syslog or webhook we support mTLS. For Splunk/HEC or Kafka we can enable SASL/SSL. We also support payload-level encryption for extra confidentiality.
[05:39] Omar: Anything about immutable storage? Can logs be tamper-evident?
[05:44] Sam: We offer signed manifests and sequence numbers. For highest assurance customers we can integrate an append-only ledger and periodic hash anchoring (e.g., publish hash to an external notarization service) — that's available as an enterprise feature.
[06:00] Alex: Quick note on metadata — we include request latency, model version, route id, and whether the request hit cache vs cold path. That helps debugging production incidents.
[06:12] Dina: Will that metadata include token-level cost details?
[06:15] Priya: Yes, token counts and cost buckets are available in operational logs, but cost-level logs are separate from PII-sensitive traces. You can control retention independently.
[06:25] Matt: How long do you retain access logs in the console UI vs exports?
[06:29] Priya: Console access logs are shorter (90 days by default) but exports can be configured for long-term retention. We recommend exporting to your own S3 for long-term archival and meeting compliance SLAs.
[06:41] Omar: Do you support syslog RFC 5424?
[06:44] Priya: Yes, syslog conforms to standard formats and we can include the JSON payload as message body for structured logging.
[06:52] Dina: What about role separation for Redwood staff access to customer logs?
[06:56] Sam: Redwood internal access is RBAC-controlled and audited. We have a break-glass process with approvals and recorded sessions for urgent support. All access by Redwood employees is recorded in your audit stream so you can review.
[07:10] Matt: If we deploy Redwood Private on-prem, how does audit logging change?
[07:15] Priya: In Private deployments, logs stay in your environment by default; our control plane can be configured to send only metadata if desired. You manage KMS/HSM and SSO locally so you control keys and residency.
[07:28] Dina: For dedicated/reserved deployments, is there any difference?
[07:32] Priya: Dedicated still uses Redwood managed control plane unless you choose Private. Audit capture is the same but export endpoints and key ownership differ. We'll include an architecture diagram.
[07:44] Omar: Any sample retention policy you recommend for banks?
[07:48] Alex: Common is 7 years for security-sensitive events, 1-3 years for operational admin logs, and 90 days for console UI access — but we can customize to meet your compliance.
[07:59] Matt: Questions from compliance: can you redact or mask PII automatically from logs?
[08:05] Sam: We support automated redaction rules at ingestion and can hash or tokenize fields. For PII in prompts we recommend redaction pre-ingest or use a PII filter pipeline. This can be applied to exported artifacts as well.
[08:19] Dina: How granular is audit searching? We need to show evidence of who changed roles in a timeframe.
[08:24] Priya: Our console supports full-text search and fielded queries over audit indices and you can query via API. Exports preserve structured fields so you can index in Splunk/Elastic for fast searches.
[08:36] Omar: Are you able to push alerts to our SOAR on specific admin events?
[08:40] Priya: Yes, we can forward event triggers to webhooks or your SOAR via connector and include the raw event for enrichment.
[08:47] Alex: Final recap: we'll send SOC2, log schema, architecture diagram with region details, and a POC plan to forward logs to Verdant Kafka cluster.
[08:57] Matt: Thanks. If you can get the signed manifest examples and ingestion test plan that would be great.
[09:02] Sam: I'll attach the signed manifest examples and include HSM options.
[09:08] Alex: Let's set a technical deep dive next week for the POC. Priya, can you own scheduling?
[09:13] Priya: Yep, I'll send calendar invites.

End transcript (timestamps approximate, transcription has occasional mis-hearings and speaker attribution may be off).
